messages:
nora_cs: Quick alert  BlueHorizon onboarding failing nightly CI. They run 14 matrix runners and see burst 429s right at cold start. Also a handful of 401s during token rotation and one 503 proxied spike.

ev an_eng: Can we get a tiny sanitized log snippet?

nora_cs: From their GH Actions job: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer eph.bh.9f3
Content-Type: application/json

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 02:03:11 GMT
Retry-After: 7
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","context":"preflight_concurrency"}
```
They also have logs showing `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` when multiple runners attempted to mint ephemeral tokens at the same instant, and a single `503 Service Unavailable` with edge-id `edge-114b`.

leo_onboard: Pattern: each runner does an SDK init that triggers preflight + separate ephemeral mint -> auth + preflight multiplied by #runners. When retries are immediate they amplify.

ev an_eng: Two quick approaches we recommend: (A) local token-broker + lockfile approach per matrix job, or (B) a tiny one-step issuer that uploads a short-lived artifact. The lockfile broker is lower-latency and avoids artifact roundtrips.

nora_cs: Customer prefers the lockfile broker but asked for a small, copy-paste example and retry guidance.

ev an_eng: Minimal lockfile broker pattern (Linux/GHA friendly):
```
# issuer.sh (run once, job-level)
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/ephemeral -d '{"aud":"ci"}')
mkdir -p /github/workspace/.tmp
echo "$TOKEN" >/github/workspace/.tmp/redwood_token
# create lockfile so only one process mints
```
and runner snippet:
```
# runner.sh
while ! ln -s /github/workspace/.tmp/lock.$JOBID /github/workspace/.tmp/lock 2>/dev/null; do
  sleep $((RANDOM%3 + 1))
done
TOKEN=$(cat /github/workspace/.tmp/redwood_token)
# use TOKEN for SDK calls
rm /github/workspace/.tmp/lock || true
```
This avoids racey mint attempts.

leo_onboard: Also recommend small startup staggering (200-1200ms), and absolutely honor Retry-After headers with jittered exponential backoff. Example pseudocode: 
```
for i in 0..4:
  r = call_api()
  if r.status == 429:
    ra = int(r.headers.get('Retry-After', 2))
    sleep((2**i + rand()) * ra)
    continue
  return r
```

maya_pm: Renewal risk: BlueHorizon has a partner demo in 5 days. If CI stays flaky we should escalate. Marked medium-high. Schedule enablement tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

nora_cs: I asked CS ops for a temporary dev-burst quota while they test. If approved we'll give them a 2x short-window burst for 48h.

ev an_eng: For the reported 401s during rotation: make sure minted TTLs overlap slightly when rotating (issue replacement ~10s before expiry) or use the lockfile broker so only one mint operation runs. Also check machine clock skew; add +-5s leeway if auth requires tight TTL.

leo_onboard: I'll draft a tiny sample repo that implements the issuer+lockfile + GHA workflow. Will include both artifact and broker patterns so customers can pick.

ci-helper-bot: Ticket CS-ONBOARD-3781 created for BlueHorizon CI preflight 429s and token-churn (priority: high).

maya_pm: Enablement agenda: confirm token reuse, confirm stagger, verify 3 clean CI runs, decide on temporary quota bump. If still red, escalate to solutions engineering before demo.

nora_cs: BlueHorizon tried the lockfile broker and 10-minute staggered re-runs: their next 6 runs showed 0 429s, 1 transient 401 that resolved with retry. I'll leave monitoring on for 48h and update CS-ONBOARD-3781. Thanks all :thumbsup:
